study_title: Digital support systems to improve child development in Peru: A cluster-randomized controlled open label trial

reconciliation_verifications.note_on_exposure_crossover: Cluster assignment integrity is verified: no populated cluster contains mixed arm_itt assignments. This establishes cluster-level assignment integrity, but does not imply absence of individual-level exposure crossover (as documented in V1 audit, 4 Control participants had positive digital tracking).

home_visits_vs_digital.interpretation: Non-significant difference; CI spans from -0.10 to +0.16 SD.
Non-significant difference; CI spans from -0.08 to +0.19 SD.

eight_core_audit_questions_answered.q1_cluster_allocation_imbalance: Extreme allocation asymmetry: Control received 68 clusters (42.8%), Digital received 72 clusters (45.3%), while Home Visits received only 19 clusters (11.9%). Control and Digital have 3.6x and 3.8x as many clusters as Home Visits.
eight_core_audit_questions_answered.q2_cluster_size_variation: Severe cluster-size variation across all arms. Cluster sizes span from 1 to 42 participants (1 to 38 in analysis sample), with CVs between 0.48 and 0.70 across arms (overall enrolled CV = 0.6419, approx 0.642; analysis CV = 0.6450). Across the entire trial, the largest 10% of clusters (16 clusters) contain 22.84% of enrolled participants (22.99% in analysis sample). Within arms, the top deciles hold 24.5% in Control (7 clusters), 17.7% in Home Visits (2 clusters), and 24.9% in Afini (8 clusters).
eight_core_audit_questions_answered.q3_effective_sample_size_reduction: Clustering reduces effective sample size by ~40% across all arms at empirical ICC rho=0.03202 (Total DE = 1.6679, effective N = 1,475.5, 59.96%). Control effective sample size is 588.0 (60.62%), Home Visits effective sample size is 195.2 (61.57%), and Digital is 690.9 (58.85%).
eight_core_audit_questions_answered.q4_precision_relative_to_control: Digital vs Control is estimated with substantially higher precision (SE=0.045 unadj, 0.045 adj) than Home Visits vs Control (SE=0.066 unadj, 0.069 adj). Home Visits confidence intervals are 54% wider due to having only 19 clusters.
eight_core_audit_questions_answered.q5_direct_hv_vs_digital_contrast: The direct contrast shows a statistically non-significant difference in favor of Home Visits: unadjusted +0.027 SD (p=0.674; 95% CI [-0.10, +0.16]) and adjusted +0.060 SD (p=0.383; 95% CI [-0.08, +0.19]). The interval is too wide to establish which is superior.
eight_core_audit_questions_answered.q6_small_sample_inference_sensitivities: Under conservative degrees of freedom (df=18), Home Visits vs Control remains statistically significant (p=0.028 adj), but confidence interval width expands by 7.2%. The direct HV vs Digital CI widens to [-0.085, +0.204].
eight_core_audit_questions_answered.q7_realistically_detectable_effect_sizes: At empirical ICC=0.03202, Digital vs Control is adequately powered (92.4%) to detect the target 0.20 SD effect (MDE = 0.165 SD). In contrast, Home Visits vs Control is underpowered for 0.20 SD (power = 64.8%, MDE = 0.240 SD). Home Visits vs Digital has only 11% power to detect the observed 0.06 SD difference and requires an effect >= 0.236 SD for 80% power.
eight_core_audit_questions_answered.q8_equivalence_and_non_inferiority_verdi: NO. The trial DOES NOT support any claim that Digital is statistically equivalent or non-inferior to Home Visits. The non-significant p-value (p=0.38) reflects lack of precision, not equivalence. The 95% CI [-0.08, +0.19] includes both substantial Home Visits superiority (+0.19 SD) and Digital superiority (-0.08 SD), completely exceeding standard non-inferiority margins.
